label_scope: Manual assertion overlap; these labels do not establish that a review finding is a real bug.

issues.title: Recurring calendar deletions are not awaited
issues.reason: In the recurring-event branch, the async callback passed to `forEach` is not awaited. It calls `getCalendar` and then pushes each deletion into `apiDeletes`, but the later `await Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes))` runs immediately and can observe an empty array. The handler can therefore report cancellation and finish database cleanup while the recurring calendar events remain; the callback's later rejections are also outside the handler's awaited error path.
issues.suggestedFixDescription: Replace the async `forEach` with an awaited `Promise.all` (or a `for...of` loop) and await each calendar deletion before the handler proceeds; push the deletion promises directly or await the completed work before the final `Promise.all`.
issues.hypothesis: Recurring booking cancellation can return before calendar events are deleted.

issues.title: Async external cleanup is launched without being awaited
issues.reason:
Async external cleanup is launched without being awaited
Several booking cleanup paths now use `async` callbacks inside `forEach`, but `forEach` does not await the returned promises. The parent workflows can therefore continue to database completion, email notification, or HTTP response before external calendar/video operations finish.
Evidence: `handleCancelBooking.ts`, both reschedule implementations, and the bookings router all introduce `forEach(async ...)`. Their callers subsequently continue with final promise aggregation, reschedule email, or response handling without collecting those callback promises.
Business impact: Cancellation or rescheduling can report completion while external calendar events or video meetings remain undeleted, and failures can surface as unhandled promise rejections.
Also affects: packages/app-store/vital/lib/reschedule.ts, packages/app-store/wipemycalother/lib/reschedule.ts, packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings.tsx
issues.suggestedFixDescription: Replace each async `forEach` with an awaited `Promise.all`/`Promise.allSettled` or a `for...of` loop. Keep the cleanup inside the existing error boundary and only send notifications, finalize promise aggregation, or return the response after all external operations have completed.
issues.hypothesis: When an async callback reaches `await getCalendar(...)` or an external deletion, the surrounding operation proceeds immediately. A rejection also bypasses the surrounding `try/catch`, leaving cleanup failures unhandled.

issues.title: Backup codes can be replayed concurrently
issues.reason: Two concurrent login requests can read the same backup-code list before either update commits. Both find the same code, authenticate successfully, and then write the same list with that code removed. This allows a one-time backup code to authorize multiple overlapping sessions.
issues.suggestedFixDescription: Consume the code atomically: use a transaction with row locking/serializable isolation, or perform a conditional compare-and-swap update based on the previously stored encrypted value and reject the login when the update affects no rows.

issues.title: Backup-code one-time consumption is not atomic across authentication flows
issues.reason:
Backup-code one-time consumption is not atomic across authentication flows
Both backup-code flows validate the encrypted code list before writing a new value. Concurrent requests can therefore authenticate with the same supposedly single-use code.
Evidence: The login provider checks the code and then updates the user record (PRF004). The disable endpoint independently checks the same code and later clears the stored codes (PRF006, PRF039), so cross-endpoint requests can both succeed using one code.
Business impact: A backup code can authorize multiple overlapping sessions or security-sensitive 2FA-disable operations, violating the one-time-use guarantee.
Also affects: apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts
issues.suggestedFixDescription: Consume codes with a transaction using serializable isolation, row locking, or a conditional compare-and-swap update. Apply the same atomic reservation/consumption mechanism to both login and disable endpoints.
issues.hypothesis: Two overlapping login/disable requests read the same backup-code list, both find the code, and both proceed before either write becomes visible.

issues.title: Meet fallback crashes without destination calendar
issues.reason: `mainHostDestinationCalendar` is undefined when `evt.destinationCalendar` is absent or empty, but this condition dereferences `.integration` unconditionally. Meet events that previously passed through with no destination calendar now throw before event creation.
issues.suggestedFixDescription: Guard the destination calendar before reading `integration`, e.g. use optional chaining or an explicit undefined check.
issues.hypothesis: A Meet event can reach create without any destination calendar.

issues.title: Meet events without calendars now crash during event creation
issues.reason:
Meet events without calendars now crash during event creation
`EventManager` unconditionally dereferences the first destination calendar, while multiple producers now intentionally normalize a missing calendar to `[]`.
Evidence: `EventManager` reads `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` without a guard (PRF016). Payment and reminder producers emit `[]` when no calendar exists (PRF023, PRF029, PRF032), and the updated webhook fixture also represents the empty state as `[]` (PRF052).
Business impact: Calendar event creation fails for Meet bookings without a destination calendar, causing booking confirmation or related workflows to error.
Also affects: packages/features/ee/payments/api/webhook.ts, apps/web/pages/api/cron/bookingReminder.ts, apps/web/playwright/webhook.e2e.ts
issues.suggestedFixDescription: Guard the first destination calendar before reading `integration`, for example `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration !== "google_calendar"`.
issues.hypothesis: A Meet booking created through a payment webhook, reminder flow, or equivalent path with no selected calendar reaches `EventManager` with an empty array and throws before calendar/video event creation.

issues.title: Stale credential reused across calendar references
issues.reason: `credential` is declared outside the reference loop and is not reset at the start of each iteration. After one reference resolves a credential, a later reference with a missing/invalid `credentialId` leaves the old object in `credential`; the subsequent `updateEvent(credential, ...)` therefore updates the previous calendar account instead of failing or resolving the current reference.
issues.suggestedFixDescription: Declare/reset the credential inside each loop iteration, and handle an unresolved credential without passing a prior iteration's credential to `updateEvent`.
issues.hypothesis: A booking can contain multiple calendar references and one referenced credential may no longer be available.

issues.title: Calendar updates can reuse a previous reference's credential
issues.reason:
Calendar updates can reuse a previous reference's credential
The multi-reference update loop resolves credentials from each calendar reference, but the outer `credential` variable is not reset per iteration. If a later credential cannot be resolved, the update path can pass the prior iteration's credential into `updateEvent`.
Evidence: `updateEvents` now iterates all calendar references and calls `updateEvent(credential, ...)` (PRF037). `CalendarManager` executes provider updates using the supplied credential and returns the resulting reference metadata (PRF040, PRF054), so a stale credential changes the external account targeted by the update.
Business impact: Rescheduling or updating a booking can modify the wrong user's external calendar and leave the intended calendar event unchanged.
Also affects: packages/core/CalendarManager.ts
issues.suggestedFixDescription: Declare or reset `credential` inside each reference iteration, and skip or return an explicit failure when the current reference cannot be resolved.
issues.hypothesis: A booking with multiple calendar references, where one referenced credential was deleted or unavailable, causes the later event update to target the previous calendar account rather than failing safely.

issues.title: Reminder cleanup is not awaited
issues.reason: Both cleanup calls are async, but the loop discards their promises and the handler proceeds to await only `prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes)`. The proposed implementations perform awaited database or provider operations before returning, so cancellation can return success while those operations are still pending; a serverless/request runtime may terminate the work, leaving reminders scheduled or database rows uncleared. The same issue applies to the adjacent SMS call.
issues.suggestedFixDescription: Collect the email/SMS cleanup promises and await them together with the other cancellation operations, or otherwise await each cleanup call before returning.

issues.title: Reminder cancellation is fire-and-forget across booking and workflow mutations
issues.reason:
Reminder cancellation is fire-and-forget across booking and workflow mutations
Multiple lifecycle paths invoke asynchronous reminder cleanup inside `forEach` without collecting or awaiting the returned promises. The callers then continue their database and rescheduling work as though cancellation completed.
Evidence: `handleCancelBooking.ts`, `bookings.tsx`, and `workflows.tsx` invoke the async helpers without `await`; `handleNewBooking.ts` wraps a synchronous `forEach` in `try/catch`, which cannot catch later async rejections. The helpers perform provider and Prisma operations asynchronously.
Business impact: Cancellation and workflow edits can report success while old reminders remain active or cleanup races with newly scheduled reminders.
Also affects: packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts, packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings.tsx, packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/workflows.tsx
issues.suggestedFixDescription: Map the relevant reminders to cleanup promises and `await Promise.all(...)` before continuing or returning. If failures must not abort the mutation, use `Promise.allSettled` and persist a deterministic retryable state.
issues.hypothesis: In a short-lived request or overlapping reschedule/update, the mutation can return or create replacement reminders before provider cancellation and row cleanup finish, leaving stale reminders or allowing old cleanup to race with new state.

issues.title: Cancels non-email and unscheduled reminders via SendGrid
issues.reason: The cancellation query selects every cancelled WorkflowReminder without filtering `method` or `scheduled`. SMS reminders are created with `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` and Twilio SIDs, but this flow sends those IDs to SendGrid's cancellation endpoint. Unscheduled email reminders are also created with `scheduled: false` and no `referenceId`, yet they are passed to the same endpoint. A provider error aborts the loop before queued deletions run, and the later unscheduled-email query does not exclude cancelled rows, so a cancelled unscheduled reminder can remain and be scheduled anyway.
issues.suggestedFixDescription: Restrict provider cancellation to scheduled email reminders with a SendGrid reference ID, delete cancelled unscheduled email reminders without calling SendGrid, and exclude cancelled reminders from the later scheduling query.

issues.title: Email reminder scheduler processes cancelled rows across methods and can reschedule cancelled unscheduled rows
issues.reason:
Email reminder scheduler processes cancelled rows across methods and can reschedule cancelled unscheduled rows
The scheduler's cancelled-reminder query is not constrained to scheduled email reminders with a provider reference, but the cleanup loop always calls the email provider cancellation endpoint. The same request then queries unscheduled email reminders without excluding cancelled rows.
Evidence: `scheduleEmailReminders.ts` filters only on `cancelled` and `scheduledDate`, then posts every result to `/v3/user/scheduled_sends`. `smsReminderManager.ts` stores SMS reminders in the same `WorkflowReminder` table, and the scheduler's later unscheduled-email query does not exclude `cancelled: true`.
Business impact: Wrong-provider cancellation requests can fail, and cancelled reminders may be sent or re-scheduled instead of remaining cancelled.
Also affects: packages/features/ee/workflows/lib/reminders/emailReminderManager.ts, packages/features/ee/workflows/lib/reminders/smsReminderManager.ts
issues.suggestedFixDescription: Filter cleanup to `method: EMAIL`, `scheduled: true`, and non-null `referenceId`; delete or finalize cancelled unscheduled rows locally; and add `cancelled: { not: true }` to the unscheduled scheduling query.
issues.hypothesis: A cancelled SMS reminder or an unscheduled cancelled email reminder can be sent to the email provider cancellation endpoint; after an endpoint failure, the later scheduling query can still select a cancelled unscheduled reminder and schedule it.

issues.title: Cancelled bookings still send scheduled emails
issues.reason: When a reminder has a SendGrid `referenceId`, the default path only updates `cancelled: true`; it does not call SendGrid's cancellation endpoint. The booking cancellation flow calls `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId)` without `immediateDelete`, so already-scheduled SendGrid emails remain active and can still be delivered after the booking is cancelled. Persisted cancellation state cannot stop SendGrid from sending an independently scheduled message.
issues.suggestedFixDescription: Pass `true` for `immediateDelete` from the booking-cancellation path, or otherwise cancel the SendGrid scheduled send whenever a referenced email reminder is cancelled.

issues.title: Booking cancellation marks email reminders cancelled without cancelling the provider send
issues.reason:
Booking cancellation marks email reminders cancelled without cancelling the provider send
The shared email cancellation helper has two incompatible lifecycle contracts:

- The default path only sets `cancelled: true`.
- Booking cancellation and rescheduling call that default path for reminders with provider references.

The persisted flag does not cancel an already scheduled provider email.
Evidence: `handleCancelBooking.ts` and `bookings.tsx` call `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId)` while `emailReminderManager.ts` handles that path by updating only the database row. Provider cancellation is reserved for the `immediateDelete` branch.
Business impact: Cancelled or rescheduled bookings can still send scheduled workflow emails to attendees.
Also affects: packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts, packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings.tsx
issues.suggestedFixDescription: Make the cancellation contract explicit and consistent: provider-backed reminders must call the provider cancellation API before marking or deleting the row, or pass `immediateDelete: true` from every path that requires immediate cancellation. Await the operation before completing the booking mutation.
issues.hypothesis: When a booking is cancelled, an email reminder with a non-null `referenceId` remains scheduled at the provider and can still be delivered because the cancellation callers do not pass `immediateDelete` and the helper does not issue the provider cancellation request.

issues.title: DST-crossing overrides use a stale offset
issues.reason: The offset is calculated only from `override.start` and then applied to both the start and end timestamps. If an override spans a DST transition, the organizer or invitee UTC offset can differ at `override.end`, so the generated end time is shifted by an hour and the slot duration or availability window becomes incorrect.
issues.suggestedFixDescription: Calculate the organizer and invitee offsets independently for both `override.start` and `override.end`, then convert each endpoint with its own offset.

issues.title: Override windows can disagree between slot generation and availability filtering across DST
issues.reason:
Override windows can disagree between slot generation and availability filtering across DST
`getSlots` converts both override endpoints using an offset derived only from `override.start`, while `checkIfIsAvailable` independently evaluates the resulting slot against the override boundaries in the organizer timezone. For an override spanning a daylight-saving transition, the generated end boundary can be shifted relative to the router's boundary check.
Evidence: `packages/lib/slots.ts` computes one `offset` from `override.start` and applies it to both endpoints (PRF003). `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts` later filters slots using separate date-override boundary calculations and `organizerTimeZone` (PRF002, PRF009), so the two stages do not share endpoint-specific conversion.
Business impact: Availability around DST transitions can expose missing slots or suppress valid slots, producing incorrect booking options and inconsistent behavior between generated schedules and final filtering.
Also affects: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts
issues.suggestedFixDescription: Convert `override.start` and `override.end` independently using offsets evaluated at each endpoint, and use the same converted instants in both `getSlots` and `checkIfIsAvailable`.
issues.hypothesis: When `override.start` and `override.end` have different organizer or invitee offsets, the generated slot window and the router's availability window represent different instants. Slots near the transition may therefore be emitted by `getSlots` but rejected by `checkIfIsAvailable`, or accepted outside the intended override interval.

issues.title: Returns wrong response shape
issues.reason: When syncing is enabled, this branch returns the raw `fetch` Response. The Google Calendar caller immediately reads `res?.data`, then accesses `token.access_token` and `token.expiry_date`; a native Response has no `data` property, so shared refreshes cannot produce usable credentials and can fail while updating the token. The helper must normalize the sync endpoint response to the same parsed shape expected by its callers.
issues.suggestedFixDescription: Parse and validate the sync endpoint response, then return the token payload in the same shape as the local refresh functions; also reject non-success HTTP responses.

issues.title: Credential sync uses an incompatible response contract
issues.reason:
Credential sync uses an incompatible response contract
The shared refresh path posts to the app-credential webhook and returns the native `fetch` `Response`, while the provider callers expect parsed provider token payloads or Axios-like objects. The webhook itself returns `{ message }` after persisting credentials, not refreshed OAuth tokens.
Evidence: `refreshOAuthTokens.ts` bypasses each provider refresh callback and returns the raw response (`PRF002`). The webhook endpoint updates credentials and responds with status messages rather than token data (`PRF001`). Callers immediately consume provider-specific response shapes, including Google (`PRF005`) and HubSpot, Zoho, and Webex (`PRF011`, `PRF032`, `PRF009`).
Business impact: Expired credentials cannot be refreshed reliably when sharing is enabled, breaking calendar, CRM, and video integrations and potentially persisting invalid token state.
Also affects: apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts, packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts, packages/app-store/hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts, packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts, packages/app-store/zohocrm/lib/CalendarService.ts, packages/app-store/webex/lib/VideoApiAdapter.ts
issues.suggestedFixDescription: Define one explicit sync contract: either have the endpoint return validated token data in the shape required by each caller, or make the helper parse a canonical response and merge it into each provider's stored credential. Reject non-2xx and non-token responses before persistence.
issues.hypothesis: When credential sharing is enabled, affected providers will dereference `.data` or provider-specific token fields on a native `Response` or webhook message and fail to refresh or persist usable credentials.

issues.title: Safe-parse wrapper is persisted as credential
issues.reason: `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the result of `schema.safeParse`, i.e. an object shaped like `{ success, data }`, not the parsed credential object. Persisting that return value as `credential.key` stores the safe-parse wrapper instead of the Google credential fields. Subsequent construction of this service reads `credential.key` through `googleCredentialSchema.parse`, so the refreshed credential can no longer be parsed and future authentication breaks. The caller must persist the parser's `.data` (or the helper must return the parsed data).
issues.suggestedFixDescription: Return the parsed data from `parseRefreshTokenResponse`, or unwrap its successful result here before assigning `key` and updating Prisma.

issues.title: Google persists the parser result wrapper instead of credential data
issues.reason:
Google persists the parser result wrapper instead of credential data
`parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the complete Zod `safeParse` result (`{ success, data }`), but Google stores that result directly as `credential.key`. The next Google service initialization expects `credential.key` itself to contain OAuth fields.
Evidence: The helper returns `refreshTokenResponse` directly (`PRF010`), while the Google caller assigns its return value directly to Prisma credential data (`PRF005`).
Business impact: A Google credential becomes unusable after its first refresh and future calendar operations fail until the user reconnects the integration.
Also affects: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts
issues.suggestedFixDescription: Return only the parsed `.data` from the helper, or unwrap `.data` at this call site before writing `credential.key`.
issues.hypothesis: After a successful Google token refresh, the credential row contains the parser wrapper rather than `access_token`, `refresh_token`, and expiry fields, causing subsequent credential parsing and authentication to fail.

issues.title: Refresh response shape causes token refresh failure
issues.reason: When `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED`, `refreshOAuthTokens` returns the native `fetch` `Response` object directly (`packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:6-14`). This caller still accesses `tokenInfo.data.error` and later `tokenInfo.data.access_token`, but a `Response` has no `data` property. Expired Bigin credentials therefore throw while checking `tokenInfo.data.error` instead of refreshing successfully.
issues.suggestedFixDescription: Normalize the shared helper's result to the Axios-like `{ data }` shape expected here, or update this caller to parse the fetch response with `await tokenInfo.json()` before reading the token payload.

issues.title: One refresh caller sends a credential ID as a user ID
issues.reason:
One refresh caller sends a credential ID as a user ID
`refreshOAuthTokens` treats its third argument as the Cal.com `userId` and sends it as `calcomUserId`. Zoho Bigin passes `credentialId`, unlike the other updated callers that pass `credential.userId`.
Evidence: The helper parameter is named `userId` and serializes it as `calcomUserId` (`PRF002`). Bigin supplies `credentialId` (`PRF040`), while Office 365 video supplies `credential.userId` (`PRF006`), demonstrating inconsistent identifier routing.
Business impact: Credential synchronization can be applied to the wrong account or fail during Bigin token refresh, creating authentication outages and cross-account credential corruption risk.
Also affects: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts, packages/app-store/office365video/lib/VideoApiAdapter.ts
issues.suggestedFixDescription: Pass the owning `userId` to the shared helper, or change the sync contract to explicitly accept and resolve a credential ID. Use distinct parameter names and types so the two identifiers cannot be mixed.
issues.hypothesis: For a Bigin credential refresh with sharing enabled, the sync request targets a credential primary key as though it were a user ID, so the receiving application can update the wrong user's credential or fail to find the intended account.

issues.title: Retry cleanup deletes other reminder methods
issues.reason: The new second OR branch is not constrained by `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS`. Therefore any workflowReminder with `retryCount > 1` is deleted whenever this SMS endpoint runs, including reminders for other delivery methods and potentially future reminders. This is destructive cross-method data loss caused by the changed cleanup predicate.
issues.suggestedFixDescription: Constrain the retry-count branch to SMS reminders (and preserve any intended scheduling-state predicate) before deleting.
issues.hypothesis: The retry-count cleanup can delete non-SMS workflow reminders.

issues.title: Global retry counter is consumed by SMS cleanup without a method boundary
issues.reason:
Global retry counter is consumed by SMS cleanup without a method boundary
The schema and migration add `retryCount` to every `WorkflowReminder`, but the SMS scheduler's retry cleanup applies `retryCount > 1` as an unscoped `OR` branch. Non-SMS reminders therefore participate in an SMS-specific destructive cleanup operation.
Evidence: `schema.prisma` and the migration define `retryCount` on the shared `WorkflowReminder` model/table, while `scheduleSMSReminders.ts` includes an `OR` branch containing only `retryCount: { gt: 1 }`; the method predicate exists only in the other branch.
Business impact: Running the SMS reminder job can permanently delete email or future delivery-method reminders after their retry count exceeds one.
Also affects: packages/prisma/schema.prisma, packages/prisma/migrations/20240508134359_add_retry_count_to_workflow_reminder/migration.sql
issues.suggestedFixDescription: Move `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` outside the `OR`, or add the method predicate to every retry-cleanup branch so the shared retry column cannot cause cross-method deletion.
issues.hypothesis: When an email or other non-SMS reminder has `retryCount > 1`, running this endpoint deletes it even if its method and schedule do not match the SMS cleanup contract.

issues.title: URL uploads bypass configured size limits
issues.reason: Every API URL upload now buffers up to 10 MB regardless of `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb`. The new downsizing block only runs for files recognized as images; non-images, unrecognized images, and failed image detection retain the full downloaded payload. `Upload.create_for` validates the upload only after this download, so deployments with smaller configured limits can be forced to download and process oversized payloads repeatedly, increasing request/job memory, disk, and bandwidth usage.
issues.suggestedFixDescription: Apply an explicit download bound appropriate to the upload type and configured attachment/image limits before buffering the remote response. Do not rely solely on the later `Upload.create_for` validation for non-image URL uploads.

issues.title: Upload size contract is inconsistent across client, remote download, and server validation
issues.reason:
Upload size contract is inconsistent across client, remote download, and server validation
The upload pipeline hard-codes a 10 MB limit in multiple layers while server-side image processing uses `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb`. This creates incompatible effective limits rather than one shared upload contract.
Evidence: The controller downloads remote uploads with `10.megabytes`, conditionally downsizes images against `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb`, and then creates the upload. The client independently sets `maxSizeKB` to `10 * 1024` for local checks and HTTP 413 messaging, so the layers disagree whenever the setting differs from 10 MB.
Business impact: Deployments with non-default image limits either reject valid uploads in the browser, accept and process oversized requests unnecessarily, or display an incorrect maximum to users; remote non-image uploads can also consume the fixed 10 MB allowance before validation.
Also affects: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js
issues.suggestedFixDescription: Define the effective per-type limit once and use it consistently for client validation, 413 messages, remote download bounds, and server-side validation. Apply an explicit bound before buffering remote uploads, including non-image types.
issues.hypothesis: If `max_image_size_kb` is below 10 MB, remote URLs and browser uploads can transfer or attempt to process data above the configured limit; if it is above 10 MB, the browser rejects files the server could accept. Non-image URL uploads are not covered by the downsizing path.

issues.title: Legacy downsize calls now raise ArgumentError
issues.reason: Ruby does not overload methods by arity: this later `downsize` definition replaces the preceding `downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` definition. The existing `Jobs::ResizeEmoji` caller still invokes `OptimizedImage.downsize(path, path, 100, 100, opts)`, so emoji resizing now raises `ArgumentError` instead of resizing. This is a runtime regression for that job.
issues.suggestedFixDescription: Keep a single `downsize` entry point that accepts both the existing `(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts)` form and the new dimension-string form, or update every legacy caller before replacing the old signature.

issues.title: Changed downsize API breaks existing emoji resize callers
issues.reason:
Changed downsize API breaks existing emoji resize callers
The new four-argument `downsize` definition replaces the preceding five-argument definition in Ruby. The existing emoji resize job still calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(path, path, 100, 100, opts)`, creating an incompatible cross-file API contract.
Evidence: `OptimizedImage` now defines `downsize` with `(from, to, dimensions, opts={})`, while the Stage 1 cross-file caller evidence identifies `app/jobs/regular/resize_emoji.rb:14` as using `(path, path, 100, 100, opts)`.
Business impact: Emoji resize jobs fail at runtime instead of producing resized emoji images.
Also affects: app/jobs/regular/resize_emoji.rb
issues.suggestedFixDescription: Preserve a single `downsize` entry point compatible with both signatures, or update every existing caller to pass a dimension string before releasing the API change.
issues.hypothesis: When `Jobs::ResizeEmoji` runs, Ruby dispatches to the new method and raises `ArgumentError` because the legacy caller supplies five arguments.

issues.title: Handle missing TopicUser records
issues.reason: `TopicUser.find_by` can return nil when a logged-in user unsubscribes from a topic they have not previously subscribed to. The next line dereferences `tu.notification_level`, causing the endpoint to raise instead of completing the unsubscribe request.
issues.suggestedFixDescription: Handle a missing TopicUser record before dereferencing it, or use a nil-safe lookup and return an appropriate successful response when no subscription exists.

issues.title: Email unsubscribe GET link mutates notification state
issues.reason:
Email unsubscribe GET link mutates notification state
The generated unsubscribe URL is exposed as a `GET` email link, but the target action immediately changes the user's `TopicUser` notification state. Email security scanners, link previews, or browser prefetching can therefore unsubscribe users without an intentional click.
Evidence: `Topic#unsubscribe_url` appends `/unsubscribe` (PRF014); `UserNotifications` places that URL into every notification email (PRF009); `config/routes.rb` registers the endpoint as `get` (PRF007); and `TopicsController#unsubscribe` assigns and saves `tu.notification_level` (PRF013).
Business impact: Automated email-link fetching can silently alter notification preferences, causing users to stop receiving topic notifications and generating support incidents.
Also affects: config/routes.rb, app/mailers/user_notifications.rb, app/models/topic.rb
issues.suggestedFixDescription: Use a non-mutating `GET` that renders a confirmation page, and perform the state change through an explicit `POST`/`PUT` action protected by the normal CSRF and authorization checks.
issues.hypothesis: A client that fetches the emailed `GET /t/:topic_id/unsubscribe` URL will execute `TopicsController#unsubscribe` and persist the notification-level change.

issues.title: Domain regex is not anchored
issues.reason: The regex searches for `@(configured domains)` anywhere in the email instead of requiring the configured domain to be the complete domain portion. With a whitelist containing `example.com`, an address such as `user@example.com.evil` still matches and is accepted, bypassing the domain restriction. The same construction also makes a blacklist for `example.com` reject suffix domains such as `user@example.com.evil`, so the validation policy is incorrect in both modes.
issues.suggestedFixDescription: Match the domain boundary/end of the email explicitly and escape configured domain values (while preserving the setting's intended domain-list syntax), rather than using an unanchored substring regex.

issues.title: User email policy accepts domains beyond the configured boundary
issues.reason:
User email policy accepts domains beyond the configured boundary
`User` routes changed email validation through `EmailValidator`, whose domain regex is unanchored. A configured `example.com` whitelist therefore accepts `user@example.com.evil`, bypassing the intended provider restriction; blacklist behavior is likewise over-broad.
Evidence: `app/models/user.rb` invokes `validates :email, email: true`, and `lib/validators/email_validator.rb` constructs `@(configured domains)` without a domain end boundary.
Business impact: Whitelist restrictions can be bypassed, allowing registrations from domains that administrators intended to reject.
Also affects: app/models/user.rb
issues.suggestedFixDescription: Escape each configured domain and require the domain portion to end at the email boundary, for example with an anchored `@(?:domain1|domain2)\z` match while preserving the setting's list syntax.
issues.hypothesis: An attacker registers with a suffix domain that contains the configured domain. Because the regex searches for a substring after `@` rather than matching the complete domain, the model validation passes when it should fail.

issues.title: Concurrent matches lose count updates
issues.reason: `should_block?` reads, increments, and later saves `match_count` as separate operations. Two concurrent calls can read the same count and both save the same incremented value, losing one match from the persisted counter. This makes the tracking data incorrect under normal concurrent signup or validation traffic.
issues.suggestedFixDescription: Update the counter atomically or lock the record across the read-modify-write operation, while preserving the timestamp update.

issues.title: Persisted blocked-email match counters lose concurrent validations
issues.reason:
Persisted blocked-email match counters lose concurrent validations
`BlockedEmail.should_block?` performs a non-atomic read-modify-save of the integer `match_count` introduced by the migration. Concurrent validations can overwrite one another's increments.
Evidence: The model increments `match_count` in memory and saves the record, while the migration defines `match_count` as a persisted integer counter with no atomic update mechanism.
Business impact: Blocked-email monitoring and operational statistics report fewer matches than actually occurred under normal concurrent traffic.
Also affects: db/migrate/20130724201552_create_blocked_emails.rb
issues.suggestedFixDescription: Update `match_count` atomically (and set `last_match_at` in the same database update), or lock the row around the read-modify-write transaction.
issues.hypothesis: Two signup or validation requests match the same blocked email concurrently, both read the same counter, increment locally, and save the same result. The persisted statistics then undercount matches.

issues.title: Non-HTTP URLs bypass SSRF validation
issues.reason: `invalid_host?` compares only `URI(@embed_url).host` with the configured host and never requires an HTTP(S) scheme. A URI such as `file://<configured-host>/...` therefore passes this check. The called importer uses `open(url).read` (app/models/topic_embed.rb:45-48), so this path can read local files or access other URI schemes instead of restricting retrieval to web URLs. This is an exploitable SSRF/local-resource access issue at the changed call site.
issues.suggestedFixDescription: Require an HTTP or HTTPS scheme before invoking the remote importer, and reject all other URI schemes.

issues.title: Untrusted embed URLs can reach remote retrieval without scheme validation
issues.reason:
Untrusted embed URLs can reach remote retrieval without scheme validation
The controller accepts a caller-supplied `embed_url` and enqueues it for background retrieval. `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?` checks only the parsed host, then `TopicEmbed.import_remote` passes the URL to `open(url).read`.

A non-HTTP URI using the configured host can therefore pass the host check and reach the remote importer, violating the boundary that should restrict retrieval to web resources.
Evidence: `app/controllers/embed_controller.rb` enqueues the untrusted parameter; `app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb` forwards it to `TopicRetriever`; `lib/topic_retriever.rb` validates only `URI(@embed_url).host`; `app/models/topic_embed.rb` performs `open(url).read`.
Business impact: An attacker can cause the application worker to access resources through unsupported URI schemes, potentially exposing local files or internal services.
Also affects: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb, app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb, app/models/topic_embed.rb
issues.suggestedFixDescription: Parse the URL once and require `http` or `https` before host validation and before calling `open`. Reject every other scheme in both the job boundary and importer.
issues.hypothesis: A URI such as `file://<configured-host>/...` passes the host comparison and is opened by the importer, allowing local-resource access or unintended URI-scheme handling.

issues.title: Remote feed HTML is stored as raw HTML
issues.reason: Feed content is controlled by the remote feed and is passed directly to `TopicEmbed.import`. That method appends it to the post and creates the post with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` (`app/models/topic_embed.rb:12,21`), bypassing normal HTML sanitization. A malicious or compromised feed can therefore inject stored script or other unsafe markup into topics viewed by users.
issues.suggestedFixDescription: Sanitize feed content before importing it, or create the post using the normal safe cooking path rather than `raw_html`.

issues.title: Remote feed content bypasses sanitization and is rendered as trusted HTML
issues.reason:
Remote feed content bypasses sanitization and is rendered as trusted HTML
Feed-controlled content flows directly from `PollFeed` into `TopicEmbed.import`, which creates or revises posts using the `raw_html` cook method. The embed view then emits `post.cooked` with `raw`.

This creates a complete cross-service trust bypass: remote feed HTML is persisted without the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline and later executed in the embed page.
Evidence: `PollFeed` passes feed content to `TopicEmbed.import` (`PRF011`); `TopicEmbed.import` creates raw-HTML posts and revisions (`PRF001`); `Post#cook` returns raw content for that method (`PRF029`); the embed view renders it with `raw` (`PRF006`).
Business impact: Users viewing imported discussions can receive stored XSS from the configured remote feed, including script execution in the forum's embed origin.
Also affects: app/models/topic_embed.rb, app/models/post.rb, app/views/embed/best.html.erb
issues.suggestedFixDescription: Sanitize imported content at the trust boundary, or route imported posts through the normal safe cooking pipeline. Do not render feed-controlled content with `raw` unless it has been proven sanitized.
issues.hypothesis: A compromised or malicious RSS/Atom feed containing executable HTML is imported and subsequently rendered to users through the embed endpoint.

issues.title: Uses full referrer as target origin
issues.reason: `request.referer` is normally a full embedding-page URL such as `https://example.test/article`, including a path. `Window.postMessage` requires `targetOrigin` to be a serialized origin, not a URL with a path; browsers therefore reject this call (and a missing referrer also yields an invalid empty target). As a result, the resize notification is not sent and the embed height contract fails for normal embeds.
issues.suggestedFixDescription: Derive and pass only the embedding page's origin, validating it before calling postMessage; skip the message when no valid origin is available.

issues.title: Embed resize producer and consumer use incompatible postMessage origins
issues.reason:
Embed resize producer and consumer use incompatible postMessage origins
The iframe layout sends the resize message using the full HTTP referrer, including its path, as `targetOrigin`. The browser messaging API requires a serialized origin, not a full URL. The parent script separately filters messages against the Discourse origin.

As a result, normal embeds do not receive the resize message, so the iframe height contract is broken.
Evidence: `EmbedController` requires a referrer (`PRF003`); the layout uses that full referrer as the `postMessage` target (`PRF016`); the parent embed script expects messages from the Discourse origin and applies the height only after receiving one (`PRF002`).
Business impact: Embedded discussions remain at the wrong iframe height, causing clipping or excess whitespace for consumers.
Also affects: app/assets/javascripts/embed.js, app/controllers/embed_controller.rb
issues.suggestedFixDescription: Derive and validate the referrer's origin, pass only `scheme://host[:port]` to `postMessage`, and keep the parent-side exact-origin and source checks aligned with that value.
issues.hypothesis: For a normal referrer such as `https://example.com/article`, the browser rejects the `postMessage` call because `https://example.com/article` is not a valid target origin.

issues.title: Flex layout targets the wrong container
issues.reason: The header markup places `.title` and `.panel` inside `.row`, while the new flex declarations are applied to their parent `.contents`. Consequently, `.panel` is not a flex item, so its new `margin-left: auto` and `order: 3` have no effect; with its float removed, it can render as a block below the title instead of remaining aligned to the right. Apply flex layout to `.row` (the container of `.title` and `.panel`) or retain an equivalent layout on that element.
issues.suggestedFixDescription: Move the flex container declarations from `.contents` to `.row`, or otherwise make `.row` a flex container so the title and panel participate in the intended layout.

issues.title: Header flex container does not contain the ordered panel
issues.reason:
Header flex container does not contain the ordered panel
The flex mixin is applied to `.contents`, but the header’s `.title` and `.panel` are children of `.row`. Therefore `.panel` is not a flex item, so its `margin-left: auto` and `order` declarations cannot perform the intended right-aligned layout.
Evidence: `header.scss` applies `@include flexbox()` to `.contents` (PRF002), while the panel receives `margin-left: auto` and `@include order(3)` (PRF003). The flex mixin only emits `display` declarations (PRF001), so it does not make the nested `.row` a flex container.
Business impact: The header panel can drop below or otherwise fail to align with the title, breaking the header layout across supported viewport sizes.
Also affects: app/assets/stylesheets/common/foundation/mixins.scss
issues.suggestedFixDescription: Apply `@include flexbox()` and alignment to `.row`, the element containing `.title` and `.panel`, or preserve an equivalent layout on `.row` before relying on the panel’s flex-item properties.
issues.hypothesis: When the header renders, removing the panel float while leaving `.row` non-flex causes the panel to participate in normal block flow rather than aligning beside the title.

issues.title: Website host bypasses privacy restriction
issues.reason: `website_name` is added as a public attribute, but it is not included in `untrusted_attributes`, unlike `website`. The attempted conditional method is also named `include_website_name` rather than the serializer convention `include_website_name?`, so it does not provide the expected inclusion guard. As a result, anonymous users can receive the host derived from a TL0 user's otherwise-hidden website, leaking profile information.
issues.suggestedFixDescription: Apply the same privacy restriction as `website` to `website_name` and define the correctly named `include_website_name?` predicate if conditional inclusion is needed.

issues.title: Public frontend exposes website host despite website privacy restriction
issues.reason:
Public frontend exposes website host despite website privacy restriction
`website_name` is exposed as a serializer attribute without the privacy restriction applied to `website`, and the profile template renders it directly via `model.website_name`. This creates a cross-layer privacy leak for users whose website is otherwise hidden from anonymous viewers.
Evidence: `app/serializers/user_serializer.rb` adds `:website_name` to the serialized attributes, while `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/templates/user/user.hbs` consumes `model.website_name` for display. The serializer does not place `website_name` under the existing website privacy restriction, and `include_website_name` is not the serializer's conditional inclusion hook name.
Business impact: Anonymous users can learn the host or path of a profile website that should remain private, causing unintended disclosure of user profile information.
Also affects: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/templates/user/user.hbs
issues.suggestedFixDescription: Apply the same privacy restriction to `website_name` as to `website`, and rename the predicate to `include_website_name?` if conditional inclusion is required.
issues.hypothesis: When an anonymous viewer loads a profile for a low-trust user with a website, the serializer includes the derived host and the template displays it, revealing profile information that `website` was intended to hide.

issues.title: Concurrent inserts can exceed device limit
issues.reason: The limit is checked with a separate COUNT before the subsequent INSERT/UPSERT. If two requests for different device IDs observe the same count below the limit, both proceed and insert, allowing the configured device limit to be exceeded. This remains possible across concurrent requests and service instances because no transaction or database-enforced capacity constraint covers the check and write together.
issues.suggestedFixDescription: Make the capacity check and new-device insertion atomic, using an appropriate transaction/locking strategy or a database-backed mechanism that enforces the limit under concurrent requests.

issues.title: Device limit is not enforced atomically across the authentication flow
issues.reason:
Device limit is not enforced atomically across the authentication flow
The anonymous authentication path uses the configured `AnonDBStore`, but capacity checking and device creation remain separate database operations.

- Concurrent requests can observe the same count below the limit.
- Both requests can then insert different devices.
- The configured device limit can therefore be exceeded, including across service instances.
Evidence: `ProvideAnonymousDeviceService` constructs the store with `cfg.AnonymousDeviceLimit` (PRF006), and `Anonymous.Authenticate` invokes `TagDevice` synchronously (PRF004). The store checks the count separately before its write (PRF001), leaving the cross-layer registration path vulnerable to concurrent over-allocation.
Business impact: More anonymous devices than configured can be registered, defeating the device cap and potentially increasing resource usage or bypassing the intended abuse-control boundary.
Also affects: pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/impl.go, pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/client.go
issues.suggestedFixDescription: Make the capacity check and new-device insertion atomic in `AnonDBStore`, using a transaction with appropriate locking or a database-backed allocation/constraint mechanism. Preserve the existing-device update path while ensuring concurrent service instances cannot exceed the limit.
issues.hypothesis: When concurrent anonymous authentications call `TagDevice`, both reach the shared store's `CountDevices` check before either insertion commits. Without a transaction, lock, or database-enforced capacity mechanism, both writes succeed and exceed the configured limit.

issues.title: Denial cache key is ambiguous
issues.reason: The key joins `name` and `parent` with `_` without escaping or length-prefixing. For example, `(name="a_b", parent="c")` and `(name="a", parent="b_c")` produce the same key for the same namespace, user, and action. `Check` uses this key to cache a denial and returns false immediately on a hit (pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:93-159). `validateCheckRequest` copies request Name and Folder directly into the check request (pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:199-230), so these delimiters are not normalized away. A denial for one resource/folder combination can therefore incorrectly deny another request until the short TTL expires.
issues.suggestedFixDescription: Build the key with an unambiguous encoding of each component (for example, length-prefix or JSON encoding) and update/add key tests covering delimiter-containing names and folders.
issues.codeSnippet: return namespace + ".perm_" + userUID + "_" + action + "_" + name + "_" + parent

issues.title: Denial-cache key collisions can cause incorrect authorization denials
issues.reason:
Denial-cache key collisions can cause incorrect authorization denials
The denial-cache key concatenates request components without escaping or length-prefixing. Distinct `(name, parent)` pairs containing underscores can produce the same key, allowing a denial cached for one resource/folder combination to be reused for another request.
Evidence: `cache.go` constructs the ambiguous key, while `service.go` checks that key and immediately returns a denial on a cache hit. For example, `(name="a_", parent="b")` and `(name="a", parent="_b")` generate the same suffix.
Business impact: Users may be incorrectly denied access to authorized resources or folders for the cache TTL, producing authorization failures based on another request's decision.
Also affects: pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go
issues.suggestedFixDescription: Encode the tuple unambiguously, such as with length-prefixed fields or structured serialization, and add tests covering delimiter-containing names and parent folders.
issues.codeSnippet: return namespace + ".perm_" + userUID + "_" + action + "_" + name + "_" + parent
issues.hypothesis: If one request is denied and cached, a distinct request with colliding component boundaries will hit `permDenialCache` in `Check` and return `Allowed: false` without re-evaluating authorization.

issues.title: Nil requests can panic middleware
issues.reason: Each instrumented method dereferences req.PluginContext before forwarding the request. If the client middleware receives a nil request, this causes a production panic instead of preserving the underlying handler behavior. The adjacent LoggerMiddleware explicitly handles nil requests for these same endpoints, confirming that nil request values are an expected middleware boundary case.
issues.suggestedFixDescription: Return directly to the next middleware when req is nil before calling instrumentContext in each instrumented endpoint method.

issues.title: Contextual middleware panics before downstream nil-request handling
issues.reason:
Contextual middleware panics before downstream nil-request handling
The newly inserted contextual logger dereferences `req` before forwarding the request. The downstream `LoggerMiddleware` explicitly handles nil requests, but middleware ordering causes the new layer to panic first, changing the established boundary behavior.
Evidence: `contextual_logger_middleware.go` dereferences `req.PluginContext` in each instrumented endpoint, while `logger_middleware.go` contains nil-request handling for the same endpoints. `CreateMiddlewares` registers the contextual logger before the logger middleware.
Business impact: Malformed or optional nil requests can crash the plugin middleware chain instead of being safely forwarded or handled, causing request failures and possible process instability.
Also affects: pkg/services/pluginsintegration/clientmiddleware/logger_middleware.go
issues.suggestedFixDescription: Add a nil-request guard in each contextual middleware method, or centralize the guard in a shared helper, and forward directly to `m.next` when `req == nil`.
issues.hypothesis: When any plugin client endpoint receives a nil request, `ContextualLoggerMiddleware` panics while accessing `req.PluginContext`, so downstream middleware and the underlying client never receive the request.

issues.title: Federated rules are treated as editable
issues.reason: The post-change implementation hardcodes `isFederated` to false, so `immutableRule` no longer protects federated rules. Federated ruler rules can therefore receive Update/Delete abilities when the user has the ordinary permissions, even though the surrounding comment states that federated rules must not be edited or removed. This regresses authorization behavior for every federated rule reaching `useAllRulerRuleAbilities`.
issues.suggestedFixDescription: Restore federated-group detection for the supplied rule/group identifier and include that result in `immutableRule` before calculating update and delete abilities.

issues.title: Federated rules remain actionable through shared ability consumers
issues.reason:
Federated rules remain actionable through shared ability consumers
`useAllRulerRuleAbilities` hardcodes federated rules as mutable. Both `RuleActionsButtons.V2` and `AlertRuleMenu` consume these abilities to expose update, delete, pause, restore, and permanent-delete actions, so the authorization regression propagates across multiple UI paths.
Evidence: `useAbilities.ts` sets `isFederated` to `false` before calculating `immutableRule` (`PRF023`). `RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx` and `AlertRuleMenu.tsx` use the resulting abilities to determine actionable controls (`PRF004`, `PRF011`).
Business impact: Users may edit, pause, delete, or permanently delete federated rules through UI paths that should treat them as immutable.
Also affects: public/app/features/alerting/unified/rule-list/components/RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx, public/app/features/alerting/unified/components/rule-viewer/AlertRuleMenu.tsx
issues.suggestedFixDescription: Restore federated-group detection for the supplied rule and group identifier, and include it in `immutableRule` before deriving all mutation abilities.
issues.hypothesis: A federated rule reaching either action component can receive enabled mutation abilities when ordinary folder permissions are present, allowing unsupported modifications through the list or rule menu.

issues.title: Async replication inherits canceled request context
issues.reason: The legacy writes run in goroutines but derive their timeout context directly from the request context. Once the API request returns, that context may be canceled, causing the legacy Create, Delete, Update, or DeleteCollection to abort immediately and leaving the two stores divergent. The timeout should be based on a context detached from request cancellation while preserving only the intended values.
issues.suggestedFixDescription: Create the asynchronous replication context from a cancellation-independent parent, then apply the ten-second timeout.
issues.codeSnippet: ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, time.Second*10, errors.New("legacy create timeout"))

issues.title: Asynchronous legacy replication can be canceled with the completed API request
issues.reason:
Asynchronous legacy replication can be canceled with the completed API request
Mode 3 returns after writing unified storage, then starts legacy replication using the request context. API request cancellation can therefore abort the background write before the ten-second timeout, leaving the stores divergent.
Evidence: `dualwriter_mode3.go` launches legacy writes in goroutines and derives their timeout contexts directly from `ctx`; `playlist_test.go` configures Mode 3 with the legacy feature toggle across file, unified, and etcd storage paths.
Business impact: Successful API requests can leave unified and legacy storage inconsistent, causing later reads, migration checks, or fallback paths to observe missing or stale playlist data.
Also affects: pkg/tests/apis/playlist/playlist_test.go
issues.suggestedFixDescription: Derive the background replication context from a cancellation-independent parent, while explicitly preserving only required request values, then apply the ten-second timeout.
issues.codeSnippet: ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, time.Second*10, errors.New("legacy create timeout"))
issues.hypothesis: When the handler context is canceled after the synchronous unified-store operation returns, the goroutine's derived context is canceled and the legacy operation fails. The playlist integration paths enable Mode 3 and legacy dual writes, so this affects production-configured replication.

issues.title: Legacy update recomputes the update independently
issues.reason: Storage.Update is called with the original UpdatedObjectInfo and returns the object selected or produced by storage, but the legacy call receives the original objInfo again. For an UpdatedObjectInfo implementation that computes or consumes the update, the second invocation can produce a different object or observe different state, so the legacy store may not receive the object committed to storage. The previous implementation explicitly materialized the updated object and wrapped it for both writes.
issues.suggestedFixDescription: Materialize the updated object once and pass a wrapper containing that exact result to the legacy update, or otherwise reuse the object returned by the storage update.
issues.codeSnippet: _, _, errObjectSt := d.Legacy.Update(ctx, name, objInfo, createValidation, updateValidation, forceAllowCreate, options)

issues.title: Mode 3 update paths can commit different payloads to the two stores
issues.reason:
Mode 3 update paths can commit different payloads to the two stores
Unified storage and legacy storage each receive the original `UpdatedObjectInfo`. If that object computes or consumes update state, the second invocation can produce a different object from the one committed by unified storage.
Evidence: The implementation passes `objInfo` independently to both `Storage.Update` and `Legacy.Update`; Mode 3 playlist integration tests exercise the dual-write configuration, while the Mode 3 unit test configures separate update expectations without asserting the object delivered to either backend.
Business impact: The two storage backends can contain different versions of the same playlist after a successful update, producing inconsistent reads and unreliable migration or recovery behavior.
Also affects: pkg/tests/apis/playlist/playlist_test.go, pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3_test.go
issues.suggestedFixDescription: Materialize the updated object once, use that exact result for both writes, or pass a wrapper to legacy storage that reuses the object committed by unified storage.
issues.codeSnippet: _, _, errObjectSt := d.Legacy.Update(ctx, name, objInfo, createValidation, updateValidation, forceAllowCreate, options)
issues.hypothesis: A playlist update through the Mode 3 integration configuration can cause unified storage to persist one computed result while the asynchronous legacy update computes another result or observes different state. The unit test mocks only return values and does not verify payload equivalence.

issues.title: Disables passkeys for initial login
issues.reason: `authenticate()` invokes `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())` before challenging the form. For the normal username/password entry path, `context.getUser()` is null, so this new predicate returns false and `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context)` is skipped. The login form therefore lacks the conditional-passkey setup on the initial request, preventing browsers from offering discoverable passkeys until a user has already been selected, which defeats the username-first conditional passkey flow. The same guard also suppresses setup for challenges where no user is present.
issues.suggestedFixDescription: Allow conditional passkey setup whenever the authenticator exists and passkeys are enabled; do not require a preselected user.
issues.codeSnippet: return webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled() && user != null;

issues.title: Initial conditional passkey setup is suppressed
issues.reason:
Initial conditional passkey setup is suppressed
`UsernamePasswordForm` now requires a preselected user before calling `fillContextForm()`. On the initial username/password request, no user is selected, so the conditional WebAuthn authenticator never receives the setup call needed to expose discoverable passkey behavior. This conflicts with the conditional authenticator's initial-login flow, where ordinary WebAuthn authenticators are intentionally hidden but conditional UI must still be initialized.
Evidence: `UsernamePasswordForm` gates `fillContextForm()` through `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())`, which returns false when the user is null (PRF016, PRF019). `WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator` disables ordinary authenticator display via `shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators()` and relies on the conditional setup path instead (PRF017, PRF026).
Business impact: Users attempting initial passwordless login with a discoverable passkey may not be offered the passkey flow until a username has already been identified, breaking username-first conditional passkey authentication.
Also affects: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authentication/authenticators/browser/WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.java, services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authentication/authenticators/browser/WebAuthnAuthenticator.java
issues.suggestedFixDescription: Allow `UsernamePasswordForm` to call `fillContextForm()` whenever the conditional WebAuthn authenticator is enabled, without requiring `context.getUser()` to be non-null. Keep user-specific authenticator listing gated separately.
issues.codeSnippet: return webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled() && user != null;
issues.hypothesis: A normal login request with passkeys enabled and no identified user skips `fillContextForm()`, preventing browser conditional passkey authentication on the initial login page.

issues.title: Sequence parsing can cross declared boundary
issues.reason: The loop only stops when `length <= 0`; it never rejects a child whose encoded size exceeds the sequence's declared content length. For example, a sequence declaring length 2 can contain a 3-byte child, causing the decoder to consume bytes outside the sequence and still return successfully. Malformed ASN.1 can therefore be accepted as a valid sequence and subsequent parsing can operate on data beyond the declared container.
issues.suggestedFixDescription: Reject any child whose encoded length exceeds the remaining sequence length, and require the remaining length to reach exactly zero before returning.

issues.title: Malformed DER can be accepted by the ECDSA signature conversion path
issues.reason:
Malformed DER can be accepted by the ECDSA signature conversion path
The DER decoder is directly used by `AuthzClientCryptoProvider` to parse ECDSA signatures, but `readSequence()` does not enforce that each child stays within the declared sequence length and also returns successfully for indefinite-length sequences. Consequently, malformed or non-DER signature encodings can be converted into concatenated `r||s` values instead of being rejected at the crypto boundary.
Evidence: `AuthzClientCryptoProvider.asn1derToConcatenatedRS()` calls `ASN1Decoder.readSequence()` and then parses the returned integers, while `readSequence()` subtracts child lengths without rejecting an overrun and skips validation when `readLength()` returns `-1`. The test suite covers only valid round trips.
Business impact: Malformed ECDSA signatures may be accepted by the conversion layer, weakening input validation and potentially causing inconsistent verification behavior across providers.
Also affects: authz/client/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authorization/client/util/crypto/AuthzClientCryptoProvider.java, authz/client/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authorization/client/util/crypto/ASN1Encoder.java
issues.suggestedFixDescription: Make the decoder strict DER: reject indefinite lengths, enforce child boundaries against the declared sequence length, require the remaining length to reach exactly zero, and add malformed-input tests through `asn1derToConcatenatedRS()`.
issues.hypothesis: An attacker-controlled or otherwise malformed ECDSA signature containing an inconsistent sequence length or indefinite-length encoding reaches `asn1derToConcatenatedRS`; the decoder accepts it or reads beyond the declared container, allowing invalid signature material to enter downstream verification.

issues.title: All-client permissions are shadowed
issues.reason: When a client-specific resource exists, evaluation uses only that resource. The fallback to the schema-wide Clients resource runs only when the specific resource is absent. AdminPermissionsSchema creates the all-clients resource during schema initialization and also supports per-client resources, so a user granted a scope on all clients can be denied access as soon as a specific resource exists without that grant. Evaluate the all-clients resource in addition to the client-specific resource, or otherwise combine both permission results.
issues.suggestedFixDescription: Evaluate permissions for both the client-specific resource and the schema-wide Clients resource, granting access when either resource grants the requested scope.

issues.title: All-client grants are ignored once a client-specific resource exists
issues.reason:
All-client grants are ignored once a client-specific resource exists
`ClientPermissionsV2` evaluates either the client-specific resource or the schema-wide `Clients` resource, but not both. Because the schema supports both resource forms, a client-specific resource can shadow an applicable all-client grant.
Evidence: `AdminPermissionsSchema` declares the `Clients` resource type and its scopes (`PRF005`), while `ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission` selects the client-specific resource and only loads the all-client resource when that lookup returns null (`PRF001`).
Business impact: Administrators with valid all-client permissions can lose access to clients as soon as client-specific authorization resources are created.
Also affects: server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authorization/AdminPermissionsSchema.java
issues.suggestedFixDescription: Evaluate both the client-specific and schema-wide `Clients` resources, granting the requested scope when either evaluation permits it.
issues.hypothesis: When a client-specific resource exists and the caller is granted a scope only through the all-client resource, `hasPermission` evaluates the specific resource, skips the fallback, and denies access despite the all-client grant.

issues.title: Deep redirect chains are truncated
issues.reason: The loop stops after 1,001 iterations even if it has not reached a terminal redirect. It then stores the new span's redirect to the intermediate `set_span_id`, so traces with more than 1,000 redirect hops can be split across multiple segment buffers instead of being merged into the final buffer. The prior implementation allowed substantially deeper chains, and the current code has no overflow handling or indication that traversal reached the limit.
issues.suggestedFixDescription: Either retain a sufficiently high traversal bound or explicitly handle an exhausted traversal by resolving the chain safely rather than committing an intermediate redirect.

issues.title: Redirect-depth reduction can split trees that the flusher treats as one segment
issues.reason:
Redirect-depth reduction can split trees that the flusher treats as one segment
The insertion script now stops redirect resolution after 1,001 iterations without detecting exhaustion. The flusher subsequently scans only the resolved segment key, so an unresolved deep redirect chain can leave spans in separate buffers.
Evidence: The loop bound was reduced from 10,000 to 1,000 and has no overflow branch. `SpansBuffer` flushes segment keys independently using `zscan`, so it cannot reunite buffers split by an incomplete redirect resolution.
Business impact: Very deep traces can be emitted as incomplete or multiple segment trees instead of one joined tree.
Also affects: src/sentry/spans/buffer.py
issues.suggestedFixDescription: Retain a safe traversal bound or explicitly handle exhaustion by resolving, rejecting, or marking the chain rather than committing an intermediate redirect.
issues.hypothesis: A trace with more than 1,000 redirect hops reaches the loop limit before its terminal segment. The script records the new span against the intermediate ID, while the flusher reads that intermediate key independently from the eventual root.

issues.title: Optimized pagination crashes on negative cursors
issues.reason: This changed line enables the paginator's advanced negative-offset path for this endpoint. In `src/sentry/api/paginator.py:877-879`, that path executes `queryset[start_offset:stop]` when `cursor.offset < 0`; the request-bound `src/sentry/utils/cursors.py:40-49` parser accepts negative offsets from a cursor string. issues.reason: The loop only stops when `length <= 0`; it never rejects a child whose encoded size exceeds the sequence's declared content length. For example, a sequence declaring length 2 can contain a 3-byte child, causing the decoder to consume bytes outside the sequence and still return successfully. Malformed ASN.1 can therefore be accepted as a valid sequence and subsequent parsing can operate on data beyond the declared container.
issues.suggestedFixDescription: Reject any child whose encoded length exceeds the remaining sequence length, and require the remaining length to reach exactly zero before returning.

issues.reason: When `readLength()` returns `-1` for an indefinite-length encoding, `while (length > 0)` is skipped and `readSequence()` returns an empty sequence without consuming or validating the end-of-contents marker. This accepts a non-DER encoding as an apparently valid empty sequence and can leave trailing sequence data to be interpreted outside its container.
issues.suggestedFixDescription: Reject indefinite-length encodings in this DER decoder, or explicitly parse and validate the end-of-contents marker and nested content boundaries.

issues.reason:

The DER decoder is directly used by `AuthzClientCryptoProvider` to parse ECDSA signatures, but `readSequence()` does not enforce that each child stays within the declared sequence length and also returns successfully for indefinite-length sequences.
